summary: Requests that RFC 1403, BGP OSPF Interaction, be moved to Historic status because the technology is no longer used.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo asks to move RFC 1403 to Historic status. It says the described BGP-OSPF interaction was not used and was complex to implement.

questions: why was bgp ospf interaction unused
why does rfc 3166 request historic status
subtitle: Requests Historic status for the BGP-OSPF interaction described in RFC 1403.

tldr.problem: The memo says the BGP-OSPF interaction in RFC 1403 was not in common use and required significant implementation complexity.
tldr.mechanism: It requests that RFC 1403 be reclassified as Historic.
tldr.outcome: The RFC records a request to retire RFC 1403 from active standards status; it is not itself a technical protocol specification.

today: RFC 3166 is an Informational memo requesting that RFC 1403 be moved to Historic status.

sections.title: The RFC 1403 Mechanism
sections.content:
RFC 1403 describes an interaction between BGP and OSPF. During a review of Internet standards related to BGP, the authors found that this mechanism was not in common use, if used at all.

The memo says implementing it would require significant complexity. It reports that the mechanism had not been used in the public Internet for many years, if ever.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier RFC described a way for BGP and OSPF to interact. The review found little or no use of that mechanism.

sections.title: Request to Reclassify RFC 1403
sections.content:
Because the interaction was not in public Internet use and added implementation complexity, RFC 3166 proposes reclassifying RFC 1403 as Historic.

The memo says moving RFC 1403 to Historic has no known effect on Internet security. It does not describe protocol changes.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors propose Historic status because the mechanism was unused and complex. They say the reclassification has no known security effect.

sections.title: Reference and Scope
sections.content:
The only protocol document cited is RFC 1403, “BGP OSPF Interaction,” published in January 1993. RFC 3166 is a short status request explaining the proposed reclassification.

The request is confined to RFC 1403. It does not define a replacement mechanism or describe changes to BGP or OSPF.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo is about the status of RFC 1403 only. It does not replace the routing protocols or define a new one.

references.text: Varadhan, K., "BGP OSPF Interaction", RFC 1403, January 1993.
